newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan engineers union says Israel arrests member.
newsitem.headline: Jordan engineers union says Israel arrests member.

text.p: Jordan's engineers union said on Wednesday one of its leading activists campaigning against normal ties with Israel was arrested by Israeli security men during a visit to the West Bank last week.

Jordan Engineers Association (JEA) said in a statement that Israel's intelligence services arrested Hatem Istanbuli last Thursday, just before he headed back to Jordan after ending a family visit "to the occupied Arab territories".
The union said Israeli authorities were not allowing any contact with Istanbuli, whom it said was being held at a prison in Jerusalem.
Istanbuli is a member of the union's "committee to resist normalisation with the Zionist enemy" and the Arab Human Rights Organisation, it said.

The Islamist-dominated union, which has more than 20,000 members, denounced Istanbuli's arrest as "a continuation of the repression and injustice which the Zionist occupation forces practice against our people and is a clear breach of all human rights covenants".

The union, which has put up a giant blackboard hung high in its offices to blacklist companies that associate with Israeli firms, is also spearheading a campaign to stop Israel's first trade fair in Jordan from going ahead later this month.
Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in October 1994 but many Jordanians still shun any contact with the Jewish state.
Popular opposition to the treaty has increased since a right-wing Israeli government came to power last May, pledging to keep captured Arab land and increase Israeli settlement.
